title: Who the Lowa Renegade Evo GTX Mid Suits, From Ngong's Mud to Mt Kenya's Scree
meta_title: Lowa Renegade Evo GTX Mid: Sturdy 590 g Boot, Who It Suits
meta_description: Lowa Renegade Evo GTX Mid explained: specs, fit, widths and the Kenyan trails it suits, plus what to check on a thrifted pair in Nairobi.
excerpt: The Lowa Renegade Evo GTX Mid is a 590 g waterproof nubuck boot in three widths. Here is how it fits, which Kenyan trails it suits and what to check on a thrifted pair.
content:
At 590 g per boot, the Lowa Renegade Evo GTX Mid is a waterproof nubuck mid-cut that suits most Kenyan hikers who want one pair for muddy day hikes near Nairobi and a few nights on Mt Kenya. It is cushioned, comes in three widths and needs little breaking in, though it runs warm on hot, dry lowland trails.

Renegades turn up on thrifted boot racks in Nairobi more than almost any other European boot. Below: what Lowa built into the Evo, how it should fit, which local trails it suits, what to check on a pre-owned pair and how to make it last.

Quick Facts

  • Weight: about 590 g per boot (men's size), per Lowa.
  • Upper and lining: nubuck leather over a GORE-TEX membrane with no intentionally added PFAS.
  • Sole unit: double-injection DuraPU/DynaPU midsole with a support frame, on a Vibram Rene Trac outsole.
  • Widths: narrow, medium and wide lasts, so broad Kenyan feet are not stuck with a pinching toe box.
  • Best Kenyan use: the Lowa Renegade Evo GTX Mid suits Ngong Hills in the short rains, the Aberdares, Mt Kenya's lower routes and two- to four-day treks.
  • Less suited to: hot, dry lowland walks such as Hell's Gate in February, where a breathable shoe is cooler.

What Is the Lowa Renegade Evo GTX Mid?

Lowa's Renegade Evo is the updated version of the company's best-selling Renegade hiking boot, a leather mid-height boot with a waterproof GORE-TEX lining. Lowa, founded in 1923 in Jetzendorf, Bavaria, pitches it at all-day trail hikes and short to moderate backpacking trips.

Think of it as a middleweight with two-zone lacing: stiffer and more supportive than a trail shoe, yet far lighter than a crampon-ready trekking boot. The cuff stands about 150 mm high outside, enough to cover the ankle bone and keep Longonot's ash out.

What changed from the classic Renegade GTX Mid?

Lowa says the Evo keeps the original's fit while cutting seams on the upper, reworking the midsole and outsole for more support and adding a little toe space. The older model used a Monowrap frame and a Vibram Evo sole, and reviewers weighed a men's UK 12 at about 700 g.

On a thrifted rack, condition matters more than generation; a well-kept classic can outlast a neglected Evo. To tell them apart, read the tongue label, which carries the word Evo on every Lowa Renegade Evo GTX Mid.

Which Kenyan Trails Suit the Renegade Evo?

The Lowa Renegade Evo GTX Mid is happiest on wet, varied ground at moderate altitude: forest paths, muddy ridges and rocky slopes between about 1,800 m and 4,000 m. It is less comfortable on long, flat, hot walks where its leather and membrane trap heat.

Day hikes near Nairobi

The Ngong Hills ridge, about an hour's drive from the CBD, turns to sticky black cotton mud in the short rains (October to December) and the long rains (March to May). A waterproof mid-cut like the Lowa Renegade Evo GTX Mid earns its keep there. Our Ngong Hills hike guide covers the route section by section.

On Mt Longonot the problem is loose ash rather than mud, and the Lowa Renegade Evo GTX Mid's cuff keeps grit away from your socks while the heel hold helps on the stepped descent back to the gate. Our Mt Longonot planning notes explain why that descent catches people out.

Mt Kenya, the Aberdares and multi-day treks

For three or four days on Mt Kenya's Sirimon or Chogoria routes, the Lowa Renegade Evo GTX Mid handles the forest, moorland and the scree below Point Lenana with a pack of around 10-12 kg. It is not insulated, so thick socks matter above 4,500 m.

Where a lighter shoe makes more sense

Hell's Gate on a dry February afternoon or Karura Forest's gentle loops rarely need a waterproof leather mid; a breathable trail shoe keeps feet cooler. If most of your hiking looks like that, the Lowa Renegade Evo GTX Mid may be more boot than you need.

How Should a Lowa Renegade Fit?

The boot should hold your heel still when laced, leave a thumb's width in front of your longest toe and let your toes wiggle freely. Lowa recommends your usual street-shoe size, tried on in the afternoon with the socks you will hike in.

Does the Renegade run true to size?

Most hikers wear their normal size in the Lowa Renegade Evo GTX Mid, but Lowa itself notes that sizing is not standardised across brands. Convert by foot length in centimetres rather than trusting a UK, US or EU label from another make; our hiking boot size chart for Kenyan buyers walks through the conversion.

A quick test: with the laces loose, slide your foot forward until the toes touch the front and fit one finger behind your heel. Then lace up and walk down a steep ramp; if your toes hit the front, go half a size up.

Narrow, medium or wide?

The Lowa Renegade Evo GTX Mid comes on narrow, medium and wide lasts (C, D and E/EE for men). Most thrifted pairs are medium, so broad-footed hikers should look for Wide on the tongue label. Cushioned merino wool hiking socks also fill small gaps.

Buying a Thrifted Pair of Renegades in Nairobi

A pre-owned Lowa Renegade Evo GTX Mid makes sense when the sole, midsole and lining still have life in them. Quality thrifted pairs bring a premium German boot within reach of hikers who would never pay the new price.

Check these points in order:

  1. Sole depth: the Vibram lugs should still have clear edges, especially under the ball of the foot and the heel.
  2. Midsole: press the side with your thumb. Fine creases are normal; deep cracks or a chalky, crumbling feel mean the polyurethane has aged.
  3. Heel counter: squeeze the back of the boot. It should spring back rather than fold.
  4. Lining: run a hand inside for holes at the heel and over the toes, where membranes usually wear first.
  5. Labels: the tongue label shows the model, size and width. The habits in our guide to spotting fake hiking boots help here too.
  6. Fit: wear your hiking socks and walk around for ten minutes before deciding.

Is the Renegade Better Than Other Boots on Our Rack?

The Lowa Renegade Evo GTX Mid is the better pick if you want cushioning, a choice of widths and a boot that stays comfortable on long, wet days. Other boots win on price or on feel for certain foot shapes, so compare a couple before you decide.

The Keen Targhee Mid waterproof boot has a roomy toe box that suits wide, flat feet, and a Quechua waterproof boot costs less for occasional day hikes. Our Lowa vs Scarpa comparison covers a narrower Italian alternative, and the hiking boot brands round-up places Lowa among the other big names.

How Do You Care for a Lowa Renegade Evo GTX Mid?

Clean the boots after every muddy hike, dry it slowly away from direct heat, and feed the nubuck with a product made for nubuck or suede. That routine keeps the leather supple and the GORE-TEX lining breathing.

Red murram dust and black cotton clay dry nubuck out, so a boot left dirty for a week can crack above the toes. Our hiking boot care routine covers the steps season by season.

Pro Tips

  • First outing: wear a newly bought Lowa Renegade Evo GTX Mid on a short Karura loop before taking them up Longonot.
  • Lacing: keep the forefoot zone relaxed and lock the top hooks firmly before a long descent.
  • Drying: remove the insoles and stuff the boots with newspaper; never dry them on a jiko or in direct sun.
  • Grass and seeds: add waterproof leg gaiters for the dew-soaked moorland on Mt Kenya.
  • Resoling: a skilled cobbler can often fit a new sole to a sound upper.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the Lowa Renegade Evo GTX Mid good for Mt Kenya?

The Renegade Evo works well for most Mt Kenya treks to Point Lenana, especially on the Sirimon and Chogoria routes, provided porters carry the heavy load. It is waterproof and supportive but not insulated, so pair it with thick merino socks and gaiters for the freezing summit morning.

How long do Lowa Renegades last?

Lowa Renegades commonly last several years of regular weekend hiking, and the leather upper usually outlives the sole. Cleaning off murram and mud after each hike, drying the boots slowly and feeding the nubuck make the biggest difference to lifespan, and a good cobbler can often resole a worn pair with a sound upper.

Do you need to break in Lowa Renegade boots?

The Lowa Renegade Evo GTX Mid needs very little breaking in, because the nubuck is soft and the fit is cushioned from the first wear. Still, walk a few hours in a newly bought pair, perhaps on a short forest loop, so the leather moulds to your feet and any rubbing shows up before a long mountain day.

Are Lowa Renegades too hot for Kenya?

Lowa Renegades can feel warm on hot, dry lowland hikes because the leather and GORE-TEX lining hold heat. On highland trails above about 2,000 m, in the rains or on early starts, the warmth is rarely a problem. Thin, wicking merino socks help, and a breathable trail shoe is a cooler choice for Hell's Gate or Lake Magadi.

What is the difference between the Renegade GTX Mid and the Evo?

The Renegade Evo GTX Mid is the newer version of the Renegade GTX Mid. Lowa reduced the seams on the upper, reworked the midsole and outsole, moved from a Vibram Evo sole to a Vibram Rene Trac sole and added a little toe room. The fit stays very close, so a good used classic is still a sound buy.

Final Thoughts

Buy this boot for comfort over distance, not for speed. The Lowa Renegade Evo GTX Mid shines on wet ridges, forest paths and the lower half of Mt Kenya, comes in three widths and asks for little breaking in, while lighter shoes stay cooler on hot lowland walks.
